items.q: What did Casey say last week that forced this demo?
items.a: A nicer Neovim is **not a GUI**. You need **arrows** and drawing that is not a text grid. A TUI **cannot layer** — one glyph per cell, no underlay.

items.q: What architecture lets TJ put GPUI on Neovim instead of forking it?
items.a: The **embed UI protocol**: Neovim stops drawing the terminal, **pushes state**, and **takes events**. FireNvim was the browser-box version of the same idea.

items.q: Which feature sold all three raters that this is a GUI?
items.a: **LSP reference arrows** drawn onto the buffer. The useful twin is a highlighted peek. Doom and Subway Surfers do **not** count — a renderer is not a GUI until it is **in the edit**.

items.q: Why does TJ care about a same-buffer markdown preview?
items.a: LLMs emit **tables** and **sequence diagrams** that are unreadable on a character grid. The preview is the **same Neovim buffer**, live — not a synced browser tab.
Keep Rust/C compiled. Put throwaway widgets in **Bun/TypeScript** so you don't rebuild the editor. When a widget is used a thousand times, **delete the JS and rewrite it in Rust**.

items.q: How does TJ stay sane while vibe-coding GPUI?
items.a: **Never read what the LLM sends back.** He will not explain how GPUI works. Ask the model. Casey *did* read Claude research prose and hated the unearned certainty.

items.q: What were the ratings, and what is Casey's scale actually measuring?
items.a: **Casey 7 / Trash 6 / Prime 6.** Five means you cannot tell TUI from GUI. Usefulness is **not** the criterion — weird drawing is. Mini-maps and 100 ms key lag are **anti-useful** and still more GUI.

items.q: How long had TJ been working on it?
items.a: Not even **10 days**. Docked panes, Linear webhooks, and browser design-mode are still missing. Emacs already has the features at **0.001 fps**.
